chapters.title: Java Foundations
chapters.description: Start from scratch — understand OOP, how Java works under the hood, and master variables & types.

chapters.title: Core Language
chapters.description: Build fluency with reference types, operators, methods, and constructors.

chapters.title: Object-Oriented Design
chapters.description: Design robust systems with classes, interfaces, and exception handling.

chapters.title: JVM Internals & Patterns
chapters.description: Go deep into memory management, garbage collection, and design patterns.

chapters.title: Modern Java
chapters.description: Master lambdas, generics, annotations, and reflection for production-grade code.

chapters.title: Foundations & Architecture
chapters.description: Hardware vs Software, Firmware, Flynn's Taxonomy, Memory Hierarchy, CPU Registers, and ISA Design.

chapters.title: Cache & Memory Hierarchy
chapters.description: Direct, Associative, and Set-Associative mapping, replacement policies (FIFO, LRU, LFU), and AMAT calculations.

chapters.title: Input/Output & Storage
chapters.description: Programmed I/O, Interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA), Disk structure, and Disk access timing.

chapters.title: Pipelining & ILP
chapters.description: 5-stage instruction pipeline, Speedup formula, Structural, Control, and Data hazards with solution mechanisms.

chapters.title: Instruction Set Design
chapters.description: 0 to 4-address instruction formats, Immediate, Direct, Indirect, Register, Relative, and Base-Index addressing modes.

chapters.title: Control Unit & Architecture Types
chapters.description: Hardwired vs Microprogrammed Control Units, Horizontal vs Vertical Microprogramming, RISC vs CISC comparison.

chapters.title: Microprocessors & Assembly
chapters.description: 8085 and 8086 architecture overview, Basic computer registers, Machine vs Assembly language, One-pass and Two-pass Assemblers.

lessons.title: OOP Fundamentals
lessons.description: Objects, Classes, Four Pillars of OOP, Relationships, Interview Prep
objectives: Understand what OOP is and why it exists
Differentiate between Procedural and OOP paradigms
Master the four pillars: Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism
Understand OOP relationships: IS-A, HAS-A, Aggregation, Composition

lessons.title: How Java Works
lessons.description: JVM, JRE, JDK, WORA principle, Compilation to Execution flow
objectives: Understand what Java is and its key characteristics
Explain WORA (Write Once, Run Anywhere)
Differentiate between JVM, JRE, and JDK
Trace the complete flow from source code to execution

lessons.title: Variables & Primitive Types
lessons.description: Primitive data types, type system, naming conventions, two's complement
objectives: Understand Java's static and strong type system
Master all 8 primitive data types with ranges and defaults
Apply variable naming conventions
Understand two's complement representation

lessons.title: Reference Types & Strings
lessons.description: Reference types, String, Arrays, Stack vs Heap, pass-by-value
objectives: Differentiate primitive types from reference types
Understand how references work in memory
Master String handling and immutability
Understand pass-by-value semantics in Java

lessons.title: Float, Double & IEEE 754
lessons.description: Floating-point representation, IEEE 754 standard, precision pitfalls
objectives: Understand IEEE 754 floating-point representation
Recognize precision issues with float and double
Know when to use BigDecimal for exact calculations

lessons.title: Control Flow Statements
lessons.description: If-else, switch cases, for loops, while loops, and jumping statements
objectives: Master decision making with if-else and switch
Understand loop structures: for, while, do-while
Use break and continue effectively

lessons.title: Operators
lessons.description: All Java operators: arithmetic, logical, bitwise, assignment, ternary
objectives: Master all categories of Java operators
Understand operator precedence and associativity
Apply bitwise operators for low-level operations

lessons.title: Methods
lessons.description: Method declaration, access specifiers, overloading, varargs, static methods
objectives: Understand complete method anatomy and declaration
Master all four access specifiers
Implement method overloading and understand static binding
Use variable arguments (varargs)

lessons.title: Constructors
lessons.description: Constructor types, this keyword, constructor chaining, copy constructors
objectives: Understand why constructors exist and how they differ from methods
Master constructor overloading and chaining
Use the this keyword effectively
Implement copy constructors

lessons.title: Types of Classes
lessons.description: Inner classes, anonymous classes, abstract classes, static nested classes
objectives: Differentiate between all types of classes in Java
Implement inner, static nested, local, and anonymous classes
Understand when to use abstract classes

lessons.title: POJO, Enum, Final & Records
lessons.description: POJO pattern, enumerations, final keyword, Java Records
objectives: Build proper POJOs following Java conventions
Master enum with methods, constructors, and fields
Apply the final keyword to variables, methods, and classes

lessons.title: Interfaces — Fundamentals
lessons.description: Interface basics, multiple inheritance, abstract vs interface
objectives: Understand what interfaces are and why they exist
Implement interfaces and achieve multiple inheritance
Differentiate between abstract classes and interfaces

lessons.title: Interfaces — Java 8/9 Features
lessons.description: Default methods, static methods, private methods in interfaces
objectives: Use default methods to add backward-compatible features
Implement static and private methods in interfaces
Resolve diamond problem with default methods

lessons.title: Exception Handling
lessons.description: try-catch-finally, checked vs unchecked, custom exceptions, throw vs throws
objectives: Understand the exception hierarchy in Java
Differentiate between checked and unchecked exceptions
Master try-catch-finally, throw, and throws
Create and use custom exceptions

lessons.title: Memory Management
lessons.description: Stack, Heap, Method Area, Garbage Collection, JVM memory model
objectives: Map the complete JVM memory model
Understand Stack vs Heap allocation
Master garbage collection algorithms and triggers
Diagnose memory leaks and optimize memory usage

lessons.title: Singleton, Immutable & Wrapper
lessons.description: Singleton pattern, immutable classes, wrapper classes, autoboxing
objectives: Implement thread-safe Singleton patterns
Design immutable classes following best practices
Master wrapper classes and autoboxing/unboxing

lessons.title: Collection Framework
lessons.description: Lists, Sets, Maps, internals of HashMap, and collection hierarchies
objectives: Master List, Set, and Map hierarchies
Understand how HashMap works internally (hashing, collision, treeifying)
Choose the right collection for the right problem

lessons.title: Queue & Comparators
lessons.description: PriorityQueues, Deques, Comparable vs Comparator interfaces
objectives: Understand Queues and Deques
Implement custom sorting with Comparable
Write flexible sorting logic using Comparator and Lambdas

lessons.title: Functional Interfaces & Lambdas
lessons.description: Functional interfaces, lambda expressions, method references, streams
objectives: Understand functional interfaces and @FunctionalInterface
Write concise code with lambda expressions
Use built-in functional interfaces: Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier
Apply method references for cleaner code

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.description: Generic classes, methods, bounded generics, wildcards, type erasure
objectives: Design type-safe generic classes and methods
Apply bounded generics with extends and super
Master wildcards: upper bound, lower bound, unbounded
Understand type erasure and its implications

lessons.title: Annotations
lessons.description: Built-in annotations, custom annotations, meta-annotations, retention policies
objectives: Understand what annotations are and why they exist
Use built-in annotations: @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings
Create custom annotations with elements and defaults
Apply meta-annotations: @Retention, @Target, @Inherited

lessons.title: Reflection
lessons.description: Reflection API, inspecting classes at runtime, dynamic method invocation
objectives: Understand what reflection is and when to use it
Inspect class metadata, fields, methods, and constructors at runtime
Invoke methods and access fields dynamically
Understand the performance implications of reflection

lessons.title: Basics of Computer Organization & Architecture
lessons.description: Hardware vs Software, Firmware, Flynn's Taxonomy, Memory Hierarchy, CPU Registers, and ISA Design
objectives: Distinguish between Computer Organization and Architecture
Understand the functional blocks of a CPU and system bus
Classify systems using Flynn's Taxonomy (SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD)
Differentiate Von Neumann and Harvard memory architectures

lessons.title: Cache Memory Organization & Mapping
lessons.description: Direct mapping, Associative mapping, Set-associative mapping, Replacement policies (FIFO, LRU, LFU), and AMAT performance formulas
objectives: Master Direct, Associative, and Set-Associative cache mapping formulas
Compute Tag, Line/Set, and Offset address fields for any cache configuration
Evaluate replacement policies (FIFO, LRU, LFU, Optimal) and trace cache hits/misses
Calculate Average Memory Access Time (AMAT) for multi-level caches

lessons.title: Input/Output Organization & DMA
lessons.description: Programmed I/O, Interrupt-driven I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA), Disk structure, and Disk access timing
objectives: Compare Memory-Mapped I/O vs Isolated (I/O-Mapped) I/O
Trace the Interrupt cycle, Daisy Chaining, and Vectored interrupts
Understand DMA transfer modes: Burst, Cycle Stealing, and Transparent
Calculate Disk Seek Time, Rotational Latency, and Data Transfer Rate

lessons.title: Pipelining & Vector Processing
lessons.description: 5-stage instruction pipeline, Speedup formula, Structural, Control, and Data hazards with solution mechanisms
objectives: Understand the 5-stage instruction pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB)
Derive Speedup, Throughput, and Efficiency formulas for pipelines
Resolve Structural, Control (Branch), and Data hazards (RAW, WAR, WAW)
Apply Operand Forwarding, Stalling, and Vector Processing principles

lessons.title: Instruction Formats & Addressing Modes
lessons.description: 0 to 4-address instruction formats, Immediate, Direct, Indirect, Register, Relative, and Base-Index addressing modes
objectives: Compare 3-address, 2-address, 1-address (Accumulator), and 0-address (Stack) formats
Calculate Effective Addresses across all basic and complex addressing modes
Select optimal addressing modes for array indexing, code relocation, and subroutines

lessons.title: Control Unit Design & RISC vs CISC
lessons.description: Hardwired vs Microprogrammed Control Units, Horizontal vs Vertical Microprogramming, RISC vs CISC comparison
objectives: Understand Hardwired control unit design (Combinational logic & State tables)
Master Microprogrammed control units, Control Memory, and Microinstructions
Differentiate Horizontal and Vertical microprogramming schemes
Perform complete architectural comparison between RISC and CISC

lessons.title: Programming the Basic Computer & 8085/8086
lessons.description: 8085 and 8086 architecture overview, Basic computer registers, Machine vs Assembly language, One-pass and Two-pass Assemblers
objectives: Understand 8085 and 8086 microprocessor internal architecture
Trace instruction code formats and basic computer registers (AR, PC, DR, AC, IR)
Explain One-Pass and Two-Pass assembler mechanics and symbol table generation
Write and trace basic assembly-language loops and subroutine calls
